If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (64)^{-}}\frac{x-8\sqrt{x}}{x-64} & =\frac{64-8\sqrt{64}}{64-64}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (64)^{-}}\frac{x-8\sqrt{x}}{x-64} & ={lim}_{x\to (64)^{-}}\frac{(x-8\sqrt{x})(x+8\sqrt{x})}{(x-64)(x+8\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (64)^{-}}\frac{{x}^{2}-{(8\sqrt{x})}^{2}}{(x-64)(x+8\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (64)^{-}}\frac{{x}^{2}-64x}{(x-64)(x+8\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (64)^{-}}\frac{x(x-64)}{(x-64)(x+8\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (64)^{-}}\frac{x}{x+8\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{64}{64+8\sqrt{64}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
